newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Coke workers ready to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Coke workers ready to end strike.

text.p: Striking workers at two Coca-Cola Co bottling plants in Sri Lanka are ready to call off their 10-week strike if the management accepts proposals put forward by the Labour Commissioner, a union leader said on Friday.

"The union is ready to accept the proposals and call off the strike," said Bala Tampoe of the Ceylon Mercantile Union. "If the other side accepts the proposals we could resume work early next week. But if they try to change them then we will have to continue the strike."

More than 700 workers are on strike at two bottling plants run by Pure Beverages Co Ltd, the island's sole local Coke bottler, a 51 percent subsidiary of F&NCC, Coke's regional bottler based in Singapore.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Labour Commissioner R. Wimalasena declined comment.
The strike, to protest against planned layoffs, has shut down Coca-Cola production in Sri Lanka since December 12.
Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga last week held separate talks with Pure Beverages management and union leaders to try to end the strike.
Union officials said the Labour Commissioner had suggested that either the number of workers to be laid off be reduced or that compensation for voluntary retrenchment be enhanced, or both.
He also suggested that the workers also be paid their bonus due in December within three days of resuming work, they said.
About 100 workers among the 350 the company wanted to lay off had already accepted the voluntary retrenchment package, Tampoe said.
Pure Beverages said recently that it had asked the government for a duty waiver to import the soft drink to meet a shortage from the strike.
The government charges a 35 percent duty on imported soft drinks.
Analysts said the strike had had no visible impact on the market as there were plenty of other soft drinks available.
Coca Cola's daily output before the strike was 40,000 cases.
